1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The gradient we are measuring now is the neutral speciation-immigration gradient, Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ = 2Jmν, so the systematic equator-to-pole increase we see is an increase in effective θ and effective immigration towards the equator. An invader that is now established at every one of the 12 sites is, in neutral terms, a single highly dispersive element of the continental metacommunity that raises the effective immigration component m for the whole guild.

That matters because the neutral richness curve is concave in θ and J. The expected absolute gain in local richness from an increase in θ or m is ΔS ≈ (∂S/∂θ)Δθ + (∂S/∂m)Δm, and ∂S/∂θ declines with S. In practice the sites that are presently species-poor and immigration-limited — Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida — sit on the steep part of the neutral curve, whereas Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui are already close to their neutral saturation expectation for the local J.

A pan-American, high-m member therefore lifts the northern, low-diversity samples toward the metacommunity mean by a larger relative amount than it can lift the already saturated equatorial samples. Zero-sum sampling means that where local richness is high the newcomer replaces rare natives by drift at a higher absolute rate, while where local richness is low the same immigration event is registered as a net gain in species detected.

The result is classic neutral homogenisation along the transect: coupling of the 12 sites to a more and more common regional pool reduces β-diversity and narrows the Seq – S high-lat difference. The mean α-diversity shifts upward everywhere but the shift is proportionally largest at high latitudes. In observational terms the positive α-diversity vs proximity-to-equator relationship remains positive for a time, but its absolute slope declines in magnitude and the equator-to-pole difference in site-level α richness is eroded.

In the long neutral equilibrium the directional component dSα/dlat is still set by the latitudinal gradient in ν and J, but the effective gradient that we will measure after the invader is at equilibrium abundance everywhere is shallower than the pre-invasion gradient. That is the neutral prediction of a flattening/homogenising latitudinal α-gradient under increased metacommunity connectivity.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The gradient we are tracking is a neutral speciation-drift-immigration gradient, not a niche competition gradient, and that is exactly why a truly cosmopolitan neutral addition will homogenise it.

Under UNTB the expectation for a local community is Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ = 2Jmν. The latitudinal increase we see now is θ(lat) and effective m(lat) being larger toward the equator, so Sα is higher in Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui than in Ottawa, State College, Charlotte.

A European insect that is now established from Ottawa to Tena is, neutrally, a high-m, highly dispersive member of the same metacommunity. Its establishment raises the effective immigration pool that every site samples from and couples the 12 localities more tightly to a shared continental pool. Because the zero-sum multinomial is concave in θ, the absolute increase in expected local richness produced by a given increase in effective immigration/metacommunity coupling is diminishing with baseline Sα. The proportional gain ΔS/S is therefore largest where S is small.

High latitude sites are the immigration-limited, drift-dominated end of the transect. They sit well below their neutral saturation expectation and therefore gain a larger relative boost from a common disperser than the equatorial sites, which are already close to the metacommunity expectation set by a larger regional θ. The north is lifted toward the south while the tropics are already near saturation, so the equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows.

That is neutral biotic homogenisation. Increased connectivity reduces β-diversity among the sites and pulls local α toward a common metacommunity mean. In the limit of complete mixing the local communities become essentially random samples of the same continental pool and the observed α-versus-latitude regression flattens, with the slope in absolute species per degree latitude declining in magnitude over time. The transient zero-sum displacement of natives is erased by drift-immigration re-equilibration, leaving a shallower, more homogeneous latitudinal α-gradient rather than a preserved additive offset.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The latitudinal alpha gradient we see now is a neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient, not a competitive one, and it is the coupling to the metacommunity that sets its steepness.

In UNTB $S_{\alpha} \simeq \theta \big[\psi(J+\theta)-\psi(\theta)\big] \approx \theta \ln[1+J/\theta]$ with $\theta =2J_{m}\nu m$, so at equilibrium local richness is a concave, saturating function of the effective metacommunity parameter $\theta$ and of the per capita immigration probability $m$. The present positive $S_{\alpha}$ vs latitude pattern is $dS/d {\rm lat}>0$ because $\theta({\rm lat})$ and effective $m({\rm lat})$ increase toward the equator, i.e. Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui are sampling a larger, less dispersal-limited regional pool than Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami.

Making one taxon truly pan-American is neutrally a massive increase in long distance coupling for the guild. It raises $m_{\rm eff}$ everywhere and it adds a high-frequency element to the regional species abundance distribution that is now drawn into every local sample. That is not a uniform +1 to every site in the zero-sum multinomial.

For a fixed local $J$ the marginal gain in expected richness from an increase in $\theta$ or $m$ is $\partial S_{\alpha}/\partial\theta =\ln[1+J/\theta]-J/(J+\theta) >0$ and is strictly decreasing in $\theta$. The proportional gain $\Delta S_{\alpha}/S_{\alpha}$ is therefore largest where $S_{\alpha}$ is initially smallest.

In zero-sum sampling the arrival of a now common widespread neutral species is balanced by stochastic loss of rare natives. The absolute loss is larger where local richness is largest, and the net neutral equilibrium moves northward toward the south. Immigration swamps local drift and the 12 localities become more tightly coupled to one common pool. Beta diversity among the transect declines and the observed $S_{\alpha}$–latitude regression attenuates.

Operationally the intercept is raised but the slope $dS_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ in absolute species per degree latitude declines in magnitude, i.e. the equator-to-pole difference in mean alpha diversity is eroded. In practice the sites that are presently species-poor and immigration-limited — Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida — sit on the steep part of the neutral curve, whereas Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui are already close to their neutral saturation expectation for the local J.

A pan-American, high-m member therefore lifts the northern, low-diversity samples toward the metacommunity mean by a larger relative amount than it can lift the already saturated equatorial samples. Zero-sum sampling means that where local richness is high the newcomer replaces rare natives by drift at a higher absolute rate, while where local richness is low the same immigration event is registered as a net gain in species detected.

The result is classic neutral homogenisation along the transect: coupling of the 12 sites to a more and more common regional pool reduces β-diversity and narrows the Seq – S high-lat difference. The mean α-diversity shifts upward everywhere but the shift is proportionally largest at high latitudes. In observational terms the positive α-diversity vs proximity-to-equator relationship remains positive for a time, but its absolute slope declines in magnitude and the equator-to-pole difference in site-level α richness is eroded.

In the long neutral equilibrium the directional component dSα/dlat is still set by the latitudinal gradient in ν and J, but the effective gradient that we will measure after the invader is at equilibrium abundance everywhere is shallower than the pre-invasion gradient. That is the neutral prediction of a flattening/homogenising latitudinal α-gradient under increased metacommunity connectivity.

The latitudinal alpha gradient we see now is a neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient, not a competitive one, and it is the coupling to the metacommunity that sets its steepness.

In UNTB $S_{\alpha} \simeq \theta \big[\psi(J+\theta)-\psi(\theta)\big] \approx \theta \ln[1+J/\theta]$ with $\theta =2J_{m}\nu m$, so at equilibrium local richness is a concave, saturating function of the effective metacommunity parameter $\theta$ and of the per capita immigration probability $m$. The present positive $S_{\alpha}$ vs latitude pattern is $dS/d {\rm lat}>0$ because $\theta({\rm lat})$ and effective $m({\rm lat})$ increase toward the equator, i.e. Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui are sampling a larger, less dispersal-limited regional pool than Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami.

Making one taxon truly pan-American is neutrally a massive increase in long distance coupling for the guild. It raises $m_{\rm eff}$ everywhere and it adds a high-frequency element to the regional species abundance distribution that is now drawn into every local sample. That is not a uniform +1 to every site in the zero-sum multinomial.

For a fixed local $J$ the marginal gain in expected richness from an increase in $\theta$ or $m$ is $\partial S_{\alpha}/\partial\theta =\ln[1+J/\theta]-J/(J+\theta) >0$ and is strictly decreasing in $\theta$. The proportional gain $\Delta S_{\alpha}/S_{\alpha}$ is therefore largest where $S_{\alpha}$ is initially smallest.

High latitude sites are immigration-limited and drift-dominated: low $\theta$, low $m$, $S_{\alpha}$ far from regional saturation. Low latitude sites are already close to their neutral expectation for a given $J$; $S_{\alpha}$ is high and the $\ln[1+J/\theta]$ curve is flat there. The same pan-American immigrant therefore lifts Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Yoro, Belmopan and Merida toward the metacommunity mean by a larger relative amount than it can lift Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui.

In zero-sum sampling the arrival of a now common widespread neutral species is balanced by stochastic loss of rare natives. The absolute loss is larger where local richness is largest, and the net neutral equilibrium moves northward toward the south. Immigration swamps local drift and the 12 localities become more tightly coupled to one common pool. Beta diversity among the transect declines and the observed $S_{\alpha}$–latitude regression attenuates.

Operationally the intercept is raised but the slope $dS_{\alpha}/d{\rm lat}$ in absolute species per degree latitude declines in magnitude, i.e. the equator-to-pole difference in mean alpha diversity is eroded. That is the classic neutral homogenisation effect of increased connectivity: a cosmopolitan neutral species makes species-poor, migration-limited northern sites catch up to species-rich tropical sites, flattening the empirical alpha diversity gradient over the remeasurement interval and tending toward a shallower, more homogeneous transect in the long dispersal limit.

The zero-sum multinomial means the invader can only be accommodated by stochastic replacement. I think the flattening argument is the one that is actually consistent with the neutral mechanics once you keep the latitudinal structure of J, m and θ in the model rather than collapsing it to a single continent-wide θ.

Under UNTB local richness is Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ = 2Jm ν. The equator-to-pole increase we see now is not a niche effect, it is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient: θ(lat) and effective m(lat) are larger toward the equator, J is on average larger and more stable there, so Sα is higher in Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado and Sarapiqui than in Ottawa, State College, Charlotte and Miami. That gradient is maintained under neutrality.

What the invasion does neutrally is increase effective connectivity for the guild. A taxon that is now present in every one of the 12 sites is by definition a very high m, essentially pan-American, member of the metacommunity. In zero-sum multinomial terms it is a constant draw from the regional species abundance distribution that is now added to the sampling at every site. Because Sα(θ) is concave, the marginal gain in local richness from an increase in θ or effective m is diminishing with baseline richness.

In absolute terms the gain is not “≈ +1 everywhere”. The expected increase ΔSα ≈ ∂Sα/∂θ Δθ + ∂Sα/∂m Δm is larger where Sα is small and immigration limited. The high-latitude sites are the drift dominated, immigration limited samples of the metacommunity. They sit on the steeply rising part of the Sα(θ) curve, so the same increase in effective immigration/metacommunity coupling lifts Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Yoro and Belmopan proportionally more than it lifts Tena and Sarapiqui, which are already close to their neutral saturation expectation for a given J.

That is the classic neutral homogenisation effect that colleagues 1, 10 and 14 are pointing to. The invader tightens coupling of the 12 localities to a common pool, β-diversity among the transect declines, and local communities are pulled toward the metacommunity mean. In practice the north catches up to the south: the absolute equator-to-pole difference in mean α-diversity narrows over re-sampling.

Zero-sum sampling also matters. The arrival of a widespread neutral species must be balanced by stochastic loss of other individuals. The expected number of rare natives lost to drift is greatest where local richness is greatest, so the tropical sites experience a larger absolute stochastic turnover even as temperate sites gain representation from the now well-mixed pool.

That does not require a competitive superiority story, it is just drift plus increased m_eff. The net observational consequence is that the positive α-diversity vs latitude relationship remains positive in sign but its magnitude attenuates: dSα/dlat loses absolute size and the α-lat slope becomes shallower and moves toward homogenisation with continued dispersal. Colleague 11 and 3 already note the panmixia limit where the gradient is eroded to zero with complete mixing; what we are seeing here is the neutral pathway toward that limit, i.e. a reduced slope, not a parallel upward shift with unchanged slope.

So I would expect a shallower, flattened α-lat gradient on re-measurement, with the greatest proportional increase in local richness at the species-poor, high-latitude end of the transect.

empty. All species in the trophic guild are demographically equivalent and
local community composition is the zero-sum multinomial sampling of a
regional metacommunity by ecological drift, immigration and in situ
speciation. Expected local richness at equilibrium is

Sα ≃ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] ,   θ = 2Jm ν ,

with J the local community size, m the per birth immigration probability
and ν the per birth speciation probability. The equator-ward increase in
site level α that you already see is therefore not a niche/competitive
gradient, it is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient
θ(lat), J(lat), m(lat). 

An insect that is now present in every part of the New World is in the
neutral picture a very high-m, highly dispersive member of the regional
pool. Ecological equivalence means its long term local frequency is set
by drift-immigration-speciation exactly as for any other member of the
guild. There is no sustained asymmetric competitive exclusion and no
systematic latitudinally biased loss of natives. In first order the
cosmopolitan taxon is simply absorbed into the regional species abundance
distribution. In absolute species numbers that is essentially a parallel
upward shift

Sα(tropics,t) ≈ Sα(tropics,0)+Δ ,    Sα(temp,t) ≈ Sα(temp,0)+Δ ,

so the absolute difference Seq–S high-lat and the sign of dSα/dlat remain
the neutral speciation driven ones: mean α remains higher towards the
equator and the directional tropical peak is not reversed or steepened by

The observed equator-to-pole increase in site-level α is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not a niche gradient. The statement “has potential to out-compete many natives” is operationally empty under neutrality; the invader can only change local frequency by drift and immigration.

Where colleagues diverge is the observable long-term effect of a now pan-American, highly dispersive neutral taxon.

Strict neutral null, argued by Colleagues 11,12,2,3,4,6,8: the invader is just one more ecologically equivalent draw. On equilibrium time scales its local abundance is set by drift-immigration-speciation exactly as for any other species. To first order Sα→Sα+Δ with Δ≈constant along the transect, a parallel upward shift of the α–latitude line. The directional speciation-driven gradient dSα/dlat>0 is maintained by the latitudinal structure of θ and m. In absolute species-number terms the regression Sα≈a+b·lat keeps b<0 essentially unchanged; any transient zero-sum displacement is erased by drift-immigration equilibration. The neutral null predicts no sustained niche-mediated steepening, reversal or permanent tropical loss.

Homogenisation reading, argued by Colleagues 1,10,13,14,5,7,9: a continent-wide high-m immigrant raises effective immigration and metacommunity coupling everywhere. Sα(θ)≈θ ln[1+J/θ] is concave, ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ)>0 and diminishing in θ. The marginal gain in expected local richness from a uniform increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα is small and immigration-limited and smallest where Sα is already near neutral saturation. High-latitude, species-poor, drift-dominated sites – Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida – are lifted toward the metacommunity mean proportionally more than already saturated equatorial sites – Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado Island, Sarapiqui. Zero-sum sampling means the invader replaces rare natives by drift at higher absolute rates where richness is high, while where richness is low the same immigration event is registered as a net gain.

Net observational consequence is neutral biotic homogenisation: β-diversity among the 12 sites declines, the equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows, and the empirical α–latitude slope loses magnitude and moves toward zero in the panmixia limit. The directional sign of the neutral speciation gradient remains in the strict θ(lat) sense, but the measured slope in species per degree latitude is attenuated; the north catches up to the tropics.

Unresolved is the operational definition of “slope”. In absolute species numbers the strict null preserves dSα/dlat set by θ(lat); in relative/proportional terms and in empirical regression the concave sampling makes the gradient appear shallower and flatter. Time-scale of drift-immigration re-equilibration vs the re-measurement interval also remains open. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 12 sites form a north–south transect with a neutral α-gradient Sα increasing toward the equator. Under Hubbell UNTB local richness is a zero-sum sample of the metacommunity, Sα≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2Jmν, J local community size, m per birth immigration, ν per birth speciation. Ecological equivalence means no species-specific competitive superiority; the European insect is operationally just another demographically equivalent draw. The observed latitudinal increase is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not niche competition.

Current round reinforces the concave-sampling / immigration-limitation mechanism. ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ)>0 and d²S/dθ²<0. A cosmopolitan, high-m invader that is now present at all 12 sites raises effective metacommunity coupling / effective m,θ for the guild everywhere. Because the neutral richness curve is concave and saturating, the absolute and especially proportional gain ΔSα from a uniform increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα is small and immigration-limited and smallest where Sα is already near neutral saturation.

High-latitude, species-poor, drift-dominated sites – Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida, Yoro, Belmopan – sit on the steep part of S(θ). Equatorial, species-rich sites – Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado Island, Sarapiqui – are close to S* for their larger tropical θ. The same pan-American immigrant therefore lifts the north toward the metacommunity mean much more than it can lift the already saturated tropics. Zero-sum sampling means the newcomer can only be accommodated by stochastic replacement; absolute stochastic loss of rare natives is larger where S is largest, reinforcing the catch-up.

Result in observational terms is neutral biotic homogenisation: β-diversity among the 12 sites falls, the equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows, the empirical Sα vs latitude regression remains positive in sign because the underlying neutral speciation gradient dS/dν>0 persists, but |dSα/dlat| in absolute species per degree latitude declines. In proportional terms the gradient is attenuated; in the idealised infinite dispersal / panmixia limit Si→Smetacommunity and the measured slope tends to zero.

The persisting disagreement is absolute-additive vs concave. Colleagues 11,3,4,8 argue in strict equilibrium language that the invasion is to first order a parallel upward shift Sα(lat)→Sα(lat)+Δ with Δ≈constant, so the directional neutral gradient dSα/dlat>0 is maintained and the absolute slope is preserved, with “flattening” being only a proportional/homogenisation statement. Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,5,7,9 stress that Δ is not constant in neutral sampling: ΔSα≈∂S/∂θ Δθ+∂S/∂m Δm declines with baseline S, so the slope magnitude is eroded even in absolute species numbers. The two statements converge if one distinguishes the speciation-driven component dS/dθ·dθ/dlat which remains, from the observable slope after increased m_eff which is shallower.

Unresolved for me: timescale of transient zero-sum displacement vs neutral drift-immigration equilibrium; whether “ultimately” means true infinite-time panmixia where latitudinal θ(lat) is swamped by continent-wide mixing, or neutral equilibrium with retained θ(lat) gradient but reduced |dS/dlat|. The common ground remains that “potential to out-compete” is neutrally meaningless, competition-mediated steepening/reversal is not predicted, and any lasting effect is homogenisation via increased connectivity and concave sampling, with greatest proportional lift at the species-poor northern end of the transect.

reflection_text.4:
The 0-round split is still the core tension. Common ground under Hubbell UNTB is settled: species are ecologically equivalent, no niche competitive superiority, local Sα is a zero-sum multinomial sample of the metacommunity set by local J, per-capita immigration m and fundamental biodiversity number θ=2Jmν. The observed equator-to-pole increase in site-level α is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not a niche gradient. The statement “has potential to out-compete many natives” is operationally empty under neutrality; the invader can only change local frequency by drift and immigration.

Where colleagues diverge is the observable long-term effect of a now pan-American, highly dispersive neutral taxon.

Strict neutral null, argued by Colleagues 11,12,2,3,4,6,8: the invader is just one more ecologically equivalent draw. On equilibrium time scales its local abundance is set by drift-immigration-speciation exactly as for any other species. To first order Sα→Sα+Δ with Δ≈constant along the transect, a parallel upward shift of the α–latitude line. The directional speciation-driven gradient dSα/dlat>0 is maintained by the latitudinal structure of θ and m. In absolute species-number terms the regression Sα≈a+b·lat keeps b<0 essentially unchanged; any transient zero-sum displacement is erased by drift-immigration equilibration. The neutral null predicts no sustained niche-mediated steepening, reversal or permanent tropical loss.

Homogenisation reading, argued by Colleagues 1,10,13,14,5,7,9: a continent-wide high-m immigrant raises effective immigration and metacommunity coupling everywhere. Sα(θ)≈θ ln[1+J/θ] is concave, ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ)>0 and diminishing in θ. The marginal gain in expected local richness from a uniform increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα is small and immigration-limited and smallest where Sα is already near neutral saturation. High-latitude, species-poor, drift-dominated sites – Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida – are lifted toward the metacommunity mean proportionally more than already saturated equatorial sites – Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado Island, Sarapiqui. Zero-sum sampling means the invader replaces rare natives by drift at higher absolute rates where richness is high, while where richness is low the same immigration event is registered as a net gain.

Net observational consequence is neutral biotic homogenisation: β-diversity among the 12 sites declines, the equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows, and the empirical α–latitude slope loses magnitude and moves toward zero in the panmixia limit. The directional sign of the neutral speciation gradient remains in the strict θ(lat) sense, but the measured slope in species per degree latitude is attenuated; the north catches up to the tropics.

Unresolved is the operational definition of “slope”. In absolute species numbers the strict null preserves dSα/dlat set by θ(lat); in relative/proportional terms and in empirical regression the concave sampling makes the gradient appear shallower and flatter. Time-scale of drift-immigration re-equilibration vs the re-measurement interval also remains open. I am retaining both the invariant directional neutral gradient and the observable neutral homogenisation/flattening as co-existing descriptions, with the flattening being the usual phrasing of the concave coupling effect.
reflection_text.3:
The problem remains a neutral theory question about a latitudinal site-level α-diversity gradient for one trophic level after a functionally equivalent European insect becomes pan-American.

Core neutral premises that are stable across rounds:
* UNTB ecological equivalence, zero-sum multinomial sampling, birth-death-immigration-speciation only. No niche/competitive superiority.
* Equilibrium local richness Sα ≈ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2Jmν. Observed equator-to-pole increase is a neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not a competition gradient.
* “Potential to out-compete” is operationally empty under neutrality. Long-term local frequency is set by drift and immigration.

Divergent interpretations that persist after round 1:

Flatten / homogenise emphasis – Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,2,5,7,9:
* A continent-wide, high-dispersal neutral taxon raises effective immigration / coupling m_eff to a common metacommunity pool everywhere.
* Sα(θ) is concave: ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ] - J/(J+θ) >0, d²S/dθ²<0. Marginal gain in local richness from an increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα and θ are small.
* High latitude sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida are immigration-limited, drift-dominated, low θ, low Sα, on the steep part of the neutral curve. Equatorial sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are near neutral saturation.
* Hence the same cosmopolitan draw lifts the north proportionally and in absolute terms more than the tropics, reduces β-diversity among the 12 sites, narrows Seq – S high-lat, and erodes the empirical α-latitude slope. In the infinite dispersal/panmixia limit Si→Smetacommunity and slope→0. Described as neutral biotic homogenisation.

Persist / essentially unchanged in absolute terms – Colleagues 11,3,4,6,8:
* Adding one neutral species is to first order a parallel upward shift Sα(lat,t)≈Sα(lat,0)+Δ with Δ≈constant along transect. The directional component dSα/dlat>0 set by θ(lat) is maintained; no sustained competitive steepening/reversal.
* No neutral mechanism for systematic latitudinally biased loss of natives. Transient zero-sum displacement at arrival is erased by drift-immigration re-equilibration.
* They acknowledge the concavity/proportional effect: constant addition is proportionally larger in species-poor north, so β diversity falls and the apparent gradient is eroded in relative terms, often phrased as flattening/homogenisation, but the absolute slope in species number per degree latitude is essentially the neutral speciation-immigration gradient.

Tension points clarified in round 1:
* Concavity of neutral sampling provides neutral basis for proportional catch-up: ∂S/∂θ declines with S, so even a uniform Δθ or Δm produces larger relative gain north.
* Disagreement is additive-constant vs proportional-convergence interpretation of the same homogenising mechanism, and whether “slope” is meant in absolute species/degree or relative/proportional terms.
* Time-scale separation remains: immediate zero-sum loss of natives where S is high vs long-term drift-immigration equilibrium.

Changes in my belief:
* Round 1 reinforces that the flattening argument is not a niche argument; it is a neutral connectivity argument via concave S(θ) and latitude-dependent immigration limitation.
* Even the persist camp now explicitly concedes proportional homogenisation and reduction in apparent slope. The strict null of no change in sign is compatible with an observable shallowing of the α-latitude regression.
* The “potential to out-compete” narrative is consistently neutralised to drift-immigration.

Unresolved:
* How much does a single pan-American species materially change effective θ vs just adding one species to the SAD? The mathematical diminishing returns argument is strong, but magnitude of Δm_eff is model-dependent.
* Whether the question asks for ultimate neutral equilibrium sign preservation vs observable slope attenuation with increased coupling.

Current working synthesis: Under strict UNTB competitive superiority is null, so no niche-driven steepening/reversal. The latitudinal α gradient is a neutral speciation-immigration gradient and its sign is preserved in the ideal neutral limit. Empirically, a cosmopolitan neutral species increases m_eff everywhere, couples the 12 sites more tightly, and because Sα(θ) is concave the gain is proportionally largest at high latitudes. This neutral homogenisation reduces β-diversity, narrows the equator-pole difference in mean α, and makes the observed α-vs-latitude slope shallower, moving toward zero in the panmixia limit. The group disagreement is essentially over phrasing of absolute parallel shift vs relative flattening; both point to neutral homogenisation with no sustained competitive loss of tropical diversity.
reflection_text.10:
The problem is 12 sites Tena ECU → Ottawa CAN with a present positive α-diversity vs proximity-to-equator gradient. An invasive European insect now occupies the whole New World guild. Question under Hubbell UNTB what happens to the slope of site-level α diversity.

Core neutral ingredients that remain stable:
* Ecological equivalence, birth-death-immigration-speciation per capita and identity-blind. No niche competitive superiority.
* Equilibrium local richness Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] or S≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] with θ=2Jmν. Present equator-pole increase is a neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not a competition gradient.
* The invader is “just another neutrally equivalent taxon”. “Potential to out-compete’’ is operationally empty in UNTB. Long term abundance is set by drift + immigration from regional pool.

Current round debate replicates previous tension but with sharper emphasis on concavity.

Flatten/homogenise camp, now 1,10,12,13,14,2,5,6,7,9:
* A pan-American high-m, high-dispersal species raises effective immigration/connectivity everywhere and couples the 12 sites to a common pool.
* Sα(θ) is concave, ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ) >0 and diminishing, d²S/dθ²<0. Marginal gain from an increase in θ/m is largest where Sα is small.
* High-latitude sites Ottawa/State College/Charlotte/Miami/Merida are immigration-limited, drift-dominated, low θ, low Sα, sit on steep part of neutral curve. Equatorial sites Tena/Cali/Barro Colorado/Sarapiqui are near neutral saturation for their J and large θ.
* Therefore a uniform increase in metacommunity coupling lifts species-poor northern sites proportionally and in practice absolutely more than saturated tropical sites. Zero-sum sampling means the newcomer replaces rare natives most in absolute terms where S is high, but net gain is felt most where S is low.
* Result: β-diversity among the transect falls, north catches up to tropics, equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows. Empirical Sα vs latitude regression remains positive in sign for a while but its absolute magnitude declines, slope becomes shallower and tends toward homogenisation / zero in the panmixia/infinite dispersal limit.

Persist/parallel-shift camp, 11,3,4,8:
* Strict neutrality predicts the latitudinal structure of α is maintained by latitudinal structure of θ(lat) and m(lat). Adding one cosmopolitan neutral species adds ≈ a constant additive offset Δ to Sα at every site, Sα→Sα+Δ.
* In absolute species numbers dSα/dlat is therefore preserved; the invasion produces at most a parallel lift of intercept, sign remains positive toward equator. Any transient displacement is erased by drift-immigration re-equilibration.
* Homogenisation is phrased as proportional effect: constant addition is proportionally larger in species-poor north, so β-diversity falls, but the directional neutral speciation gradient dS/dν>0 persists.

Tension to track:
* Concavity argument for flattening of observed absolute slope vs strict additive-constant argument for slope invariance in absolute species numbers. Both use same zero-sum multinomial, differ on whether a truly everywhere-present neutral immigrant is modelled as a uniform Δθ/Δm felt proportionally more at low S, or as +1 ecologically equivalent species.
* Role of “out-compete”. Under UNTB competitive exclusion is replaced by stochastic replacement; any short-term dip in local richness is transient.
* Unresolved nuance: is question about sign, magnitude, or proportional slope? Most colleagues now state both: sign stays positive in strict neutral null, but observed magnitude attenuates due to increased connectivity and concavity, i.e. a flattening/homogenisation of the α-latitude relationship.

My current working understanding: UNTB null is no niche-driven steepening/flattening. The directional equatorward increase in α is maintained by neutral speciation-immigration gradient. The invader is neutrally equivalent, so no sustained competitive reversal. However the concave sampling function plus latitude-dependent immigration limitation means a cosmopolitan neutral immigrant homogenises local assemblages; the proportional gain is larger in species-poor northern sites. Operationally this is reported as a shallower, flattened α-lat slope, declining in magnitude toward zero with increased mixing, while the underlying θ(lat) gradient remains the neutral driver. I am keeping both the strict slope-persistence claim in absolute terms and the homogenisation/concavity claim for the observable magnitude.
reflection_text.8:
The question is the long-term fate of the latitudinal alpha-diversity slope under Hubbell UNTB after a truly continent-wide invasive in the same trophic guild establishes from Ottawa to Tena.

Core neutral premises that remain stable:
- Ecological equivalence; birth-death-immigration-speciation are identity blind. No sustained competitive superiority. “Potential to out-compete” is niche language and neutrally empty.
- Local equilibrium Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] ~ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)], θ =2Jmν. The observed equator-to-pole increase is a neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not niche.
- An introduction is neutrally just another draw from the metacommunity. Long-term local abundance is set by drift + immigration.

Round 1 public positions:
Flattening / homogenisation emphasis: Colleagues 1, 10, 13, 14, 5, 7, 9, 2. 
Argument: A pan-American high-m taxon raises effective immigration/connectivity everywhere. Because Sα(θ,m,J) is concave, ∂S/∂θ >0 and d²S/dθ² <0, the absolute and especially proportional gain ΔS from a uniform increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα is small and immigration-limited. High-latitude sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida/Yoro/Belmopan sit on the steep part of the neutral curve, drift dominated; equatorial sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are near neutral saturation. Thus the north catches up to the tropics, β-diversity among the 12 sites falls, the equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows, and the empirical Sα vs latitude regression becomes shallower in absolute species per degree and moves toward homogenisation. Panmixia limit → S_i → Smetacommunity, slope →0.

Slope-preserved / parallel-shift emphasis: Colleagues 11, 12, 8, 3, 4, 6.
Argument: Strict neutrality gives no directional competitive exclusion. The invader is assimilated into the regional pool; equilibrium returns to Sα* = f(J,m,θ(lat)). To first order it adds ≈ one ecologically equivalent species to every local sample, Sα → Sα+Δ with Δ≈ constant along transect. The directional gradient dSα/dlat set by latitudinal θ(lat),J,m persists, sign stays positive toward the equator, absolute slope dS/dlat is maintained. Proportional homogenisation is real – the constant addition is proportionally larger at low Sα, β-diversity falls – but that is phrased as neutral homogenisation, not a change in the neutrally determined slope. Transient zero-sum displacement at arrival is erased by drift-immigration re-equilibration.

Disagreements / open points I keep:
- Additive constant vs shape change: does a continent-wide high-m species merely raise θ by ≈1 everywhere, or does it raise m_eff in a latitude-dependent way because m is limiting at high latitudes? The concave sampling makes marginal gain latitude dependent.
- Operational definition of “slope”: absolute species per degree latitude vs proportional change. Flattening camp reads the empirical regression magnitude as decreasing; preservation camp reads the neutrally determined directional component as unchanged with a parallel intercept shift.
- Transient vs equilibrium: short-term zero-sum loss largest where Sα is largest, but long neutral equilibration restores Sα(θ(lat)).
- Infinite dispersal/panmixia limit: all agree in complete mixing local assemblages converge, empirical slope →0. Dispute is whether the invasion itself moves the system meaningfully toward that limit on ecological time scales or just adds a neutral constant.

Current synthesis: UNTB null removes niche-driven competitive loss. The latitudinal gradient is maintained by θ(lat) and immigration limitation. Strictest neutral reading = slope sign and neutrally generated steepness persist with at most a parallel upward shift; homogenisation is a reduction in β-diversity and proportional convergence. The flattening argument is the concave-marginal-gain / immigration-limitation reading that the observed absolute slope will be attenuated because the same connectivity increase lifts species-poor northern sites more than species-rich equatorial sites. Unresolved for me which interpretation is the more faithful representation of the zero-sum multinomial sampling limit under a uniformly increased m_eff.
reflection_text.11:

Under Hubbell UNTB local Sα ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ], θ=2Jmν, is a zero-sum sample of the metacommunity set by local J, per-capita immigration m and fundamental biodiversity number θ. Ecological equivalence removes niche competitive superiority; the “potential to out-compete” is operationally empty neutrally.

The latitudinal Sα gradient is therefore a neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), J(lat), m(lat), not a niche gradient.

The invasive European insect, once pan-American, is neutrally one more ecologically equivalent draw with very high dispersal / large effective m. 
Flattening/homogenisation view - Colleagues 1,2,5,7,10,13,14 and now reinforced in round 1: Sα(θ) is concave, ∂S/∂θ>0, d²S/dθ²<0. A uniform increase in metacommunity coupling / effective θ/m raises expected Sα everywhere but the absolute/proportional gain ΔS is diminishing with baseline Sα. High-latitude sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida are immigration-limited, drift dominated, low θ, low Sα and sit on the steep part of the neutral curve; equatorial sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are near neutral saturation for their J. A cosmopolitan high-m immigrant therefore lifts the species-poor north toward the metacommunity mean proportionally more than it can lift the already saturated tropics. Maintenance/constant-offset view - Colleagues 2,3,4,6,8,11,12: in strict equilibrium Sα(J,m,θ(lat)) is preserved. Adding one neutral species adds essentially a constant +Δ to every local sample, Sα→Sα+Δ, so absolute differences and the sign of dS/dlat>0 persist. Under strict UNTB the speciation-driven directional component dS/dν>0 persists, which is the constant-offset argument; the commonly quoted neutral homogenisation is a proportional effect and the concave sampling effect on the observable regression magnitude. Long-term limit with a truly ubiquitous high-m species is an effective increase in coupling that reduces the θ(lat) signal in practice, even if formally θ(lat) remains.

reflection_text.12:
The transect Tena → Ottawa shows a present positive equator-ward site-level alpha richness gradient. Under Hubbell UNTB species are ecologically equivalent and local alpha is a zero-sum sample of the metacommunity: Sα ≈ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ = 2Jmν. The observed gradient is neutrally a speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not a niche competitive gradient.

The introduced European insect is pan-American and highly dispersive. In strict neutrality “potential to out-compete” is operationally meaningless; the invader is just one more demographically equivalent taxon added to the regional pool. Its long-term local abundance and incidence are set by drift and immigration, not asymmetric competition.

Current deliberation converges on neutral homogenisation via increased metacommunity coupling, with residual disagreement about how to phrase the slope change.

Homogenisation / flattening view, Colleagues 1,2,5,6,7,10,12,13,14,9:  
A cosmopolitan high-m neutral species raises effective immigration/connectivity everywhere. Because Sα(θ) is concave, ∂S/∂θ = ln(1+J/θ)-J/(J+θ) >0 and d²S/dθ²<0, the absolute gain ΔS from a uniform Δθ/Δm is largest where baseline Sα and θ are smallest. High latitude sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida are immigration-limited and drift dominated, low θ, low Sα; equatorial sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are near neutral saturation, high θ, high Sα. The north is therefore lifted proportionally and in absolute terms more than the tropics, β-diversity among the 12 sites declines and the equator-to-pole difference in mean alpha narrows. The positive α-latitude relationship remains positive in sign but its absolute slope dSα/dlat declines in magnitude, i.e. the gradient flattens / homogenises. In the panmixia limit S_i → S_metacommunity and the empirical slope tends to zero.

Slope-persistence / neutral null phrasing, Colleagues 3,4,8,11,12:  
The directional component of the gradient is set by the latitudinal gradient in θ(lat). The invader is assimilated into the regional pool and on evolutionary time scales communities relax back to Sα* = f(J,m,θ(lat)). In first order the invader adds ≈ a constant to every local sample, Sα → Sα + Δ, so the sign dSα/dlat >0 persists and the absolute species-number slope is maintained by the neutral speciation-driven gradient. The proportional effect is homogenisation: the constant addition is proportionally larger in species-poor high-latitude sites, reducing β-diversity. This is described as an intercept lift with unchanged absolute slope, versus an attenuation of the slope in absolute terms.

Unresolved / notes:  
The mathematical effect of a uniform increase in θ/m is not strictly constant; concavity implies genuine flattening of the absolute species-number slope even within neutral expectations. The core disagreement is semantic: “slope unchanged because gradient is set by θ(lat)” vs “slope flattens because ∂S/∂θ declines with θ”. Transient zero-sum displacement at arrival can transiently depress local richness where the invader first establishes, largest in absolute terms where S is largest, but this is erased at neutral drift-immigration equilibrium.

Current understanding: neutrality nulls competitive superiority; long-term latitudinal alpha is speciation-immigration driven. The consensus mechanistic prediction is a neutral homogenising effect of a ubiquitous disperser that reduces the equator-pole alpha difference, i.e. a shallower/flattened slope in practice, while strictly the directional speciation gradient remains the only persistent neutral driver and no niche-mediated steepening/reversal is predicted. The most defensible operational statement is attenuation of the magnitude of the observed α-latitude slope, with greatest proportional lift at the species-poor northern end of the transect.
reflection_text.6:
The question is a neutral null test. Under Hubbell UNTB species are ecologically equivalent, local alpha is a zero-sum multinomial sample of the metacommunity

Sα ≈ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] ,  θ = 2Jm ν

with J local community size, m per-capita immigration, ν per-capita speciation. The present equator-to-pole increase in site alpha is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not a niche/competitive gradient. The statement “potential to out-compete” is operationally empty under neutrality; the invader is just one more demographically equivalent draw.

Where colleagues diverge is how a now pan-American, high-m taxon changes the observable α–latitude relationship.

Homogenisation/flattening camp: a truly cosmopolitan neutral species raises effective m/connectivity everywhere and raises θ effectively. Sα(θ) is concave, ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ)>0 and d²S/dθ²<0, so the marginal absolute gain ΔS from a uniform increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα and θ are small. High-latitude sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida are immigration-limited, drift-dominated, low θ, low Sα and sit on the steep part of the neutral curve; equatorial sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are already near neutral saturation for their J and θ. Zero-sum sampling therefore lifts the north toward the metacommunity mean proportionally and, in practice, in absolute species number more than the south. Beta diversity among the 12 sites falls, the equator–pole difference in mean alpha narrows, and the empirical regression Sα≈a+b·lat with b<0 becomes shallower in absolute species per degree latitude and in relative terms moves toward homogenisation. In the infinite dispersal/panmixia limit Si→Smetacommunity and the measured slope →0.

Gradient-persistence camp: to first order the cosmopolitan taxon is absorbed as θ→θ+Δθ, m_eff→m_eff+Δm everywhere. In absolute species numbers that is essentially a parallel upward shift Sα(tropics,t)≈Sα(tropics,0)+Δ, Sα(temp,t)≈Sα(temp,0)+Δ, so the sign dSα/dlat>0 set by the latitudinal θ(lat) gradient is preserved and there is no neutral mechanism for a sustained niche-mediated steepening or tropical loss. The directional speciation-immigration component remains the only systematic driver.

Resolution: both statements are compatible if absolute vs proportional slope and equilibrium vs transient are distinguished. Strictly, the neutrally determined directional component dS/dν>0 persists. Operationally the concave neutral sampling function and latitudinal immigration limitation mean the constant neutral addition is experienced as a larger proportional and in practice larger absolute increase at species-poor northern sites than at species-rich equatorial sites. Transient zero-sum displacement at first arrival is erased by drift-immigration re-equilibration. The observable outcome on ecological time scales is neutral homogenisation: mean alpha rises everywhere, beta diversity declines, the north catches up to the tropics, and the measured α–latitude slope attenuates / flattens, becoming shallower in absolute magnitude and tending toward zero with complete mixing, with no sustained competitive steepening or reversal of the tropical peak.

Unresolved that still matters: magnitude of Δθ from one ubiquitous taxon relative to the standing latitudinal θ gradient; time scale of drift-immigration equilibration vs the re-survey window; and whether the report is framed as absolute slope in species/degree vs relative/proportional slope. Niche-mediated competitive loss is not predicted under strict neutrality.

The 12 sites form a north–south transect with a neutral α-gradient Sα increasing toward the equator. Under Hubbell UNTB local richness is a zero-sum sample of the metacommunity, Sα≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2Jmν, J local community size, m per birth immigration, ν per birth speciation. Ecological equivalence means no species-specific competitive superiority; the European insect is operationally just another demographically equivalent draw. The observed latitudinal increase is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not niche competition.

Current round reinforces the concave-sampling / immigration-limitation mechanism. ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ)>0 and d²S/dθ²<0. A cosmopolitan, high-m invader that is now present at all 12 sites raises effective metacommunity coupling / effective m,θ for the guild everywhere. Because the neutral richness curve is concave and saturating, the absolute and especially proportional gain ΔSα from a uniform increase in θ/m is largest where baseline Sα is small and immigration-limited and smallest where Sα is already near neutral saturation.

High-latitude, species-poor, drift-dominated sites – Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida, Yoro, Belmopan – sit on the steep part of S(θ). Equatorial, species-rich sites – Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado Island, Sarapiqui – are close to S* for their larger tropical θ. The same pan-American immigrant therefore lifts the north toward the metacommunity mean much more than it can lift the already saturated tropics. Zero-sum sampling means the newcomer can only be accommodated by stochastic replacement; absolute stochastic loss of rare natives is larger where S is largest, reinforcing the catch-up.

Result in observational terms is neutral biotic homogenisation: β-diversity among the 12 sites falls, the equator-to-pole difference in mean α narrows, the empirical Sα vs latitude regression remains positive in sign because the underlying neutral speciation gradient dS/dν>0 persists, but |dSα/dlat| in absolute species per degree latitude declines. In proportional terms the gradient is attenuated; in the idealised infinite dispersal / panmixia limit Si→Smetacommunity and the measured slope tends to zero.

The persisting disagreement is absolute-additive vs concave. Colleagues 11,3,4,8 argue in strict equilibrium language that the invasion is to first order a parallel upward shift Sα(lat)→Sα(lat)+Δ with Δ≈constant, so the directional neutral gradient dSα/dlat>0 is maintained and the absolute slope is preserved, with “flattening” being only a proportional/homogenisation statement. Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,5,7,9 stress that Δ is not constant in neutral sampling: ΔSα≈∂S/∂θ Δθ+∂S/∂m Δm declines with baseline S, so the slope magnitude is eroded even in absolute species numbers. The two statements converge if one distinguishes the speciation-driven component dS/dθ·dθ/dlat which remains, from the observable slope after increased m_eff which is shallower.

Unresolved for me: timescale of transient zero-sum displacement vs neutral drift-immigration equilibrium; whether “ultimately” means true infinite-time panmixia where latitudinal θ(lat) is swamped by continent-wide mixing, or neutral equilibrium with retained θ(lat) gradient but reduced |dS/dlat|. The common ground remains that “potential to out-compete” is neutrally meaningless, competition-mediated steepening/reversal is not predicted, and any lasting effect is homogenisation via increased connectivity and concave sampling, with greatest proportional lift at the species-poor northern end of the transect.

reflection_text.3:
The problem remains a strict UNTB neutral theory question about site-level α-diversity for one trophic level along a North–South American transect after a functionally equivalent European insect becomes pan-American.

Zero-sum sampling accommodates the newcomer by stochastic replacement of rare natives; absolute turnover largest where Sα largest, net immigration gain registered most where Sα small.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The latitudinal pattern we already have is the UNTB sampling gradient, not a niche one, and that is exactly why the re-survey will look different.

Sα ≃ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≈ θ ln[1+J/θ] with θ=2Jmν. The equator-ward increase we measure at Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui vs Ottawa, State College, Charlotte is θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat). Ecological equivalence means the European insect is just a demographically equivalent draw that, once it is at all 12 sites, is a very high-m, essentially pan-American element of the same guild.

That is a uniform increase in effective metacommunity coupling for the transect. The neutral sampling function is concave:

∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ] - J/(J+θ) >0, d²S/dθ² <0

so the marginal gain in expected local richness from an increase in θ/m is diminishing with baseline richness.

High latitude sites Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida are immigration-limited, drift-dominated, low θ, low Sα and sit on the steep part of Sα(θ). Neotropical sites Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui are already close to neutral saturation for their larger tropical θ and J and sit on the flat part.

The same cosmopolitan high-m draw therefore raises expected Sα everywhere, ΔSα>0, but ΔSα is largest in absolute and especially proportional terms where Sα is initially smallest. Zero-sum multinomial sampling accommodates the newcomer by stochastic replacement: where Sα is large the replacement is dominated by loss of rare natives to drift, where Sα is small it is registered as a net immigration gain.

The net neutral outcome is biotic homogenisation along the transect. β-diversity among the 12 sites falls, local assemblages are pulled toward a common pool mean and the north catches up to the tropics. Mean α is lifted everywhere but the equator-to-pole difference in mean site α is eroded.

Operationally that is an attenuation of the empirical regression Sα = a + b·lat. The directional neutral driver dS/dν>0 is retained in the strict θ(lat) sense, so the sign stays positive, but the observable slope in species per degree latitude loses magnitude. reflection_text.4:
The UNTB premises are settled across the group: ecological equivalence, local Sα is a zero-sum multinomial sample of the metacommunity set by J, per-capita immigration m and fundamental biodiversity number θ=2Jmν. The present equator-to-pole increase in site α at Tena, Cali, Barro Colorado, Sarapiqui vs Ottawa, State College, Charlotte, Miami/Merida is the neutral speciation-immigration-drift gradient θ(lat), m(lat), J(lat), not niche competition. The statement “potential to out-compete” is operationally empty; the invader can only change local frequency by drift/immigration.

Current round has converged on the concave-sampling homogenisation mechanism. Sα≈θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)]≈θ ln[1+J/θ] is concave, ∂S/∂θ = ln[1+J/θ]-J/(J+θ)>0, d²S/dθ²<0, with the same diminishing returns in m. A pan-American, high-m neutral taxon raises effective connectivity/coupling for the whole guild. The marginal absolute and especially proportional gain ΔSα≈∂S/∂θ Δθ+∂S/∂m Δm is largest where baseline θ and Sα are small and immigration-limited and smallest where Sα is already near neutral saturation for J.

That is exactly the latitudinal structure of the transect: high-latitude sites are drift-dominated, immigration-limited, low θ, low Sα on the steep part of Sα(θ); equatorial sites are high θ, high effective m, close to saturation on the flat part. The same cosmopolitan draw therefore lifts the species-poor north toward the metacommunity mean by a larger proportional and in practice larger absolute amount than it can lift the already saturated tropics. In zero-sum terms the newcomer is accommodated by stochastic replacement of rare natives; loss is largest in absolute terms where Sα is largest, gain is registered as net richness where Sα is small.

Net neutral outcome is biotic homogenisation: mean α rises everywhere, β-diversity among the 12 sites falls, the north catches up to the tropics and the equator-to-pole difference in mean site α narrows. Operationally the empirical Sα vs latitude regression loses magnitude: the positive sign dS/dν>0, the strict directional neutral speciation-immigration driver dSα/dlat>0 set by θ(lat), is retained in theory, but the observed slope in species per degree latitude becomes shallower, attenuates and moves toward zero in the idealised infinite dispersal/panmixia limit Si→Smetacommunity.

The earlier “parallel upward shift, slope unchanged” intuition is rejected as missing the latitude dependence of ∂S/∂θ and of m limitation; the neutral sampling function is not linear in the immigrant addition. The remaining nuance is definitional/time-scale: in strict absolute species-number terms the directional θ(lat) component formally persists, while in observable relative/proportional terms and in the usual empirical regression the gradient flattens. Time to drift-immigration re-equilibration vs the re-measurement interval remains open, but the mechanistic prediction for a future remeasurement is a shallower, more homogeneous α–latitude relationship with the greatest proportional increase at the species-poor high-latitude end.

Sα ≃ θ[ψ(J+θ)-ψ(θ)] ≃ θ ln[1+J/θ] ,  θ = 2Jmν

and the same diminishing returns holds for m. The marginal gain
ΔSα ≃ ∂S/∂θ Δθ + ∂S/∂m Δm from a uniform increase in connectivity is
therefore diminishing in baseline richness: largest where baseline θ and Sα
are small and immigration limited and smallest where Sα is already near its
neutral saturation expectation for J.

initially smallest and smallest where Sα is already near its neutral ceiling.

net immigration gain is registered where Sα is small, drift loss of rare
natives dominates where Sα is large.

species-poor north catches up to the species-rich tropics. The equator-to-pole
